title: not blazing-fast
body:
## Bug Report

#### Current Behavior
Takes over a second to load. Within this issue I'll also add two screen recordings, one with starship and other with p10k (for reference).

#### Expected Behavior
Be actually blazing-fast

#### Additional context/Screenshots
p10k for reference

[Screencast from 2024-04-09 16-56-37.webm](https://github.com/starship/starship/assets/94996251/14094207-1ca2-47f2-b981-5a328bd8d18d)

starship

[Screencast from 2024-04-09 16-57-52.webm](https://github.com/starship/starship/assets/94996251/db887e6a-9e2e-4474-92ed-a941c0cc7108)


#### Environment
- Starship version: 1.17.1
- Shell type: zsh
- Shell version: 5.9
- Terminal emulator: mate-terminal
- Operating system: nixOS

comments.author: participant2
comments.body: Ok: p10k does some async stuff, but that should affect git operations in big repos and similar stuff to be really that noticeable. This feels like the general startup of your shell is slow. If this is starship, you could try to "prerender" the init script and source that instead of sourcing the starship init call (just dump that output into a file and source it directly instead of getting it from the starship init call).

comments.body:
ugh @participant1 was right... it was my zshrc all along. these two lines to be more specific:
```sh
autoload -Uz compinit && compinit
compinit -d "$XDG_CACHE_HOME"/zsh/zcompdump-"$ZSH_VERSION"
```
